perf.summary: PushVersion takes a 'len' parameter that is completely ignored, and the Version struct it implies is never populated — dead/misleading API.
perf.currentCost: PushVersion(int* roots, ref int versionCount, int root, int len) writes only roots[versionCount++] = root; the 'len' argument is silently discarded. The Version struct (Root, Len) is declared but never stored or returned, so callers pass len believing it is recorded. This is a correctness/ergonomics hazard, not a perf cost.
perf.proposedChange: Either (a) remove the unused 'len' parameter and the Version struct if length-per-version is not a feature, or (b) actually store versions as Version*/SoA so GetVersion can return both Root and Len. Pick one to make the API honest. Current signature should not advertise a parameter it drops.
perf.rationale: Removes a silently-ignored argument that callers pay to compute and pass for no effect; makes the persistent-SAM version API self-consistent. No hot loop here, but it eliminates wasted argument setup and a misleading contract.
perf.risk: Changing the public signature is a source-break for any external caller. Grep of src shows no in-repo callers of PushVersion/GetVersion, so internal break risk is nil; confirm no Unity-side consumer before removing the parameter.

perf.summary: Both using directives in PersistentSam.cs are unused.
perf.currentCost: Neither System nor System.Runtime.InteropServices is referenced — there is no StructLayout attribute or System type in the file. Dead directives.
perf.rationale: Cleaner unit, explicit dependency surface, zero behavioral change. If [StructLayout] was intended on the Version struct for blittable Burst layout, add it explicitly instead of leaving the unused import.
perf.risk: None functionally. If the Version struct is meant to be blittable across Burst boundaries, consider adding [StructLayout(LayoutKind.Sequential)] explicitly (it is already sequential by default for this all-int struct, so no actual change needed).
